title: Latency SLO shepherding for regional routing with tiered model-variant fallbacks
creator: Devon Singh
summary: Implement a shepherding logic that selects region + tier based on p50/p95 latency and a composite network health score, and gracefully falls back to lower-cost or quantized model variants when regional health degrades.
description: Problem: Customers expect predictable tail latency (p95) while minimizing cost. Current region selection uses simple recent-p95 ranking which causes flapping during transient network perturbations and doesn't consider cross-region network health or model variant compatibility. This ticket designs and implements a decision engine that uses both p50 and p95 plus a normalized network health score to choose region + tier and trigger model-variant fallbacks when necessary. The goal is robust routing that meets latency SLOs while degrading gracefully to compatible variants (quantized or smaller families) rather than failing requests.
background: Existing work focused on single-metric region ranking (p95) and has led to oscillation under noisy telemetry. Related tickets (see dependencies) introduced composite scores and probabilistic circuit-breakers but didn't cover tier-aware routing or variant compatibility. We need a production-ready, testable policy that integrates with the runtime routing layer and Console routing controls.
proposal: 1) Compute per-region rolling metrics: p50, p95, qps, packet_loss, backend_error_rate, and capacity_headroom. 2) Normalize metrics to [0,1] per region using EWMA baselines. 3) Compute composite network_health = 0.4*(1 - packet_loss_norm) + 0.3*(1 - backend_error_norm) + 0.2*(capacity_headroom_norm) + 0.1*(1 - jitter_norm). 4) Compute latency_score = 0.6*p95_norm + 0.4*p50_norm. 5) region_score = alpha * (1 - latency_score) + beta * network_health where alpha and beta are tunable (default alpha=0.7, beta=0.3). 6) Apply hysteresis: only switch region if new_region_score - current_region_score > 0.12 and sustained for 30s. 7) Tier-aware routing: prefer tier (dedicated > hosted > private) subject to customer policy; if chosen tier lacks capacity, fall back to next tier if region_score above threshold. 8) Variant fallback matrix: define compatible fallbacks per model family (e.g., rl-13B-int8 -> rl-7B-int8 -> rl-7B-q4). When region_score < 0.4 or p95 exceeds SLO by >40%, trigger automated fallback to next compatible variant for that customer until region health recovers. 9) Provide ability to pin region/tier/variant via route config to opt-out.
metrics: variant-fallback rate (requests served by fallback models)
decision_logic:
Thresholds and pseudocode:
- Normalize metrics to 0..1 using EWMA baselines (window=5m).
- region_score = 0.7*(1 - p95_norm) + 0.3*network_health_norm.
- If region_score_candidate - region_score_current > 0.12 and sustained for 30s -> initiate warmup and route shift (gradual 10% increments over 60s).
- If p95_current_region > SLO * 1.4 OR network_health_current_region < 0.4 -> evaluate fallback variants in order.
- When triggering variant fallback, mark request metadata: routed_due_to_fallback=true and emit trace IDs.
Implementation considerations: keep decisions idempotent, store last decision timestamp, add cooldown (180s) after any switch to avoid churn.
acceptance_criteria: Region selection chooses the same top-1 region as manual offline comparator in 95% of synthetic stable scenarios
Under induced packet-loss (5% for 60s) the system switches to a healthier region within 45s and keeps p95 within 1.5x SLO for >= 80% of requests
Variant fallbacks are triggered when thresholds met and no unhandled 500s occur due to model incompatibility
Console shows per-route breakdown of active region, chosen tier, and active model variant with links to traces
Switch hysteresis and cooldown prevent flapping: measured region-switch frequency < 0.2 switches/minute in noisy tests
End-to-end tests (see test_plan) pass in staging and performance regression < 5% on stable traffic
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Simulation (this ticket): run in dry-mode for 1 week using historical telemetry to surface decision mismatches
Phase 1 - Canary (internal-only routes): enable live decisions for 5% traffic in 'experimental' route group, monitor metrics for 48 hours
Phase 2 - Customer opt-in: choose small set of low-SLA customers to opt-in; run for 7 days and iterate based on feedback
Phase 3 - Default routing: enable for all hosted routes with opt-out via route config; monitor for 14 days then promote to runtime-1.22
test_plan: Unit tests for normalization and score computation (edge cases: zero-traffic, extreme loss)
Integration: simulate multi-region telemetry feed and assert stable region selection under noise
Chaos: inject packet_loss, jitter, and backend 5xx in the active region and verify failover and fallback behavior
Compatibility: exercise fallback matrix for at least 6 model families and verify no schema/response regressions
Load: validate routing code adds <3% CPU overhead at 10k rps per routing proxy node
risks: Incorrect normalization can overweight one metric and cause bad routing decisions
Fallbacks to incompatible variants could break downstream consumers (structured output changes)
Metric delays or telemetry gaps could cause stale decisions; need explicit staleness handling
Rollout could increase cross-region egress costs as traffic moves between regions
Edge cases: cold KV cache in fallback variant may spike latency temporarily
